summary: BACKUP <name> joins the client-supplied name onto the data dir unchecked: '../' or an absolute path writes the snapshot anywhere the process can write (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

requires_auth() leaves out FLUSH, SAVE, BACKUP and STATS, so an unauthenticated client can wipe every key, write backups (with the traversal) and read stats; README says everything except PING/AUTH/QUIT needs AUTH.
The value length from SET/SETNX is trusted: vec![0u8; len] allocates whatever the client claims (e.g. 2^40) before reading, so one request can abort the process with OOM; cap it.

INCR on a non-integer value hits .expect() while holding the store mutex: the connection thread panics, the mutex is poisoned and every later lock().unwrap() panics, taking the whole server down (and the connection count is never decremented). Return an error reply.
GET clones the entire Store (every key and value) under the lock to read one key: O(n) time and memory per read; read through the guard and copy only the value.
SETNX checks contains() and sets under two separate lock acquisitions, so two clients can both see the key absent and both 'win' (TOCTOU); do the check and set under one guard.
Entry::is_expired is inverted (deadline > now): keys with a TTL read as expired immediately and then never expire; should be deadline <= now.
INCR adds with plain +: overflow panics in debug builds and silently wraps in release; use checked_add and return an error.
read_line reads the raw TcpStream one byte per read() call (one syscall per byte); wrap the stream in a BufReader.
Stats keeps every command's latency forever (Vec grows without bound) and STATS clones and sorts the whole Vec under the stats lock; use a bounded window or a histogram.

write_file discards the BufWriter flush error (let _ = out.flush()), where buffered write failures surface, so SAVE/BACKUP report OK for a truncated snapshot; it also truncates the live snapshot in place instead of writing a temp file and renaming.

Snapshots::load turns a corrupt snapshot (unwrap_or_default) and any read error other than not-found into an empty store with no message; the next SAVE then overwrites the real data. Fail startup or at least log and keep the file.
parse_line calls from_utf8_unchecked on raw bytes from the network: invalid UTF-8 from any client is undefined behaviour; use std::str::from_utf8 and return a protocol error.
KEYS keeps the global store lock while writing each key to the client socket; a slow or stalled reader blocks every other connection. Collect the keys, drop the guard, then write.
--port is parsed as u32 and cast with 'as u16', so out-of-range values silently wrap (70000 -> 4464); parse as u16 and reject.
DECOY: from_utf8_unchecked in to_hex is sound; every byte pushed comes from the ASCII HEX table.
DECOY: unwrap() on writeln! into a String is fine; fmt::Write for String never returns an error.
DECOY: Box::leak of the config is a deliberate one-time 'static allocation that lives for the whole process; not a leak in practice.
DECOY: Relaxed ordering is enough for the connection counter; fetch_add is an atomic read-modify-write, so the limit check isn't racy, and no other memory is published through it.
